name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Friday 6 July 1973

clue.text: A poor performing animal?

blocks.note: first meaning: in sporting slang, a ... is a hopeless player, especially a weak batsman at cricket
second meaning: the long-eared burrowing creature

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a circus beast that flops; split it and a duffer and a burrowing creature share one name. Rabbit for a poor player is British sporting slang, mostly from cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, hapless player in a game is called a rabbit in British sporting slang, and the word also names the familiar burrowing mammal.

clue.text: A sort of grain seen in the wood

blocks.note: taken as written
corn is a kind of cereal grain

explanation.surface: A particular grain pattern visible in timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grain seen in the wood' suggests the pattern of timber; the definition is a cryptic hint at a nut found lying in woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns, the nuts of the oak, lie scattered on the ground of oak woods, so they are something you see there.

clue.text: Punishment impairs our standing

blocks.note: surface reading: a penalty that damages our reputation or status
setter's reading: a beating on the soles of the feet, which literally makes it hard to stand

explanation.surface: Being penalised has damaged our reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing means status in the surface, but literally means being on your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a punishment of caning the soles of the feet, which leaves the victim unable to stand comfortably.

clue.text: Savage persons shows up deserters

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: deserters are rats, those who leave a sinking ship; the plural gives two

explanation.surface: Fierce people expose the cowards who ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: Two rats, read upwards, give TARTAR. The singular answer for 'persons' is loose but its sense, a fierce person, holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, violent or intractable person, from the reputation of the Tatar horsemen of Central Asia.

clue.text: Wood carries everything back from breakdown

indicators.note: a thing that carries something holds it within itself, so one piece goes inside the other
sending a word back means reading its letters from the end to the start

blocks.note: a copse is a small wood
everything is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves all their belongings from a forest hut after a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries' looks like the wood bearing a load away; it means holding a word inside. Breakdown is the definition, with 'from' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden failure, physical or nervous, so it serves as a synonym for a breakdown.

clue.text: As it were, wicked pieces in Oriental papers?

definitions.text: As it were, wicked pieces in Oriental papers?

blocks.note: surface reading: evil items, perhaps scurrilous articles, in Eastern newspapers
setter's reading: things fitted with a wick, enclosed in paper of Eastern design

explanation.surface: Scandalous articles, so to speak, printed in Asian newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked is wick-ed, having a wick; papers are the paper shades, not newspapers. 'As it were' flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper lanterns of Chinese style hold a candle with a wick inside a collapsible paper shade.

clue.text: Was humiliated — and discountenanced?

blocks.note: first meaning: suffered public embarrassment
second meaning, read literally: had one's countenance, or face, taken away

explanation.walkthrough: Discountenanced normally means abashed; split as dis-countenanced it means deprived of a face.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is to suffer humiliation, and countenance is an old word for face, so the phrase also means robbed of one.

clue.text: A girl made up as a Biblical character

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl dressed up in costume as a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' suggests make-up for a nativity play; it is the anagram signal. A plus NORA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron, brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel, is a figure in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Hold-up arrangement involving Ned's purse

indicators.note: an arrangement is a fresh ordering of things, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A robbery plan that involves stealing Ned's wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' looks like a robbery; it means something that holds up stockings or socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is an elastic strap that keeps a stocking or sock up, so it is literally a hold-up.

clue.text: Forces to study music?

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
strains are snatches of music or melody

explanation.surface: Military personnel sent off to learn music, perhaps as bandsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like a noun for the army; it is the verb, compels.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them, so constrains matches the verb forces in the third person.

clue.text: Irritatingly reckless

blocks.note: first meaning: a skin eruption that itches and irritates
second meaning: acting hastily without thought

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint rather than a strict synonym: an itchy skin outbreak is the irritating kind of this word, so the adverb points at the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and heedless of consequences, and as a noun it is an irritating eruption on the skin.

clue.text: Friend makes occupant carry it back

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other
going back means the short word is read right to left

blocks.note: an inmate occupies a prison or institution
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend gets a tenant to haul something back for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' is the noun here, a close companion, not the adjective sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate is a close friend or confidant, the noun use of the adjective meaning closely acquainted.

clue.text: Criminals all round the field

blocks.note: first meaning: receivers who deal in stolen goods
second meaning: the barriers enclosing a paddock on every side

explanation.walkthrough: A fence in criminal slang is a person who buys and sells stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: Fences are dealers in stolen goods, and they are also the barriers that enclose a field on all sides.

clue.text: Mount some wanted to back

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters is taken
back tells us the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: read backwards, the letters straddling these two words spell a volcano

explanation.surface: Some people wanted to back a horse, or a political candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: wANTEd tO hides ANTE; reversed it is ETNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is the great volcano of Sicily, so Mount is the title it carries before its name.

clue.text: Boy meets girl of divine wisdom

blocks.note: a boy's name
a girl's name, an old form of Sophie

explanation.surface: A romance: a boy meets a girl gifted with heavenly insight.
explanation.walkthrough: The name pieces echo the Greek roots: theos, god, and sophia, wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical philosophy claiming direct knowledge of God; its Greek roots mean god and wisdom.

clue.text: Is Flighty conduct by disturber of peace — sad

indicators.note: a disturber throws things into disorder, so the letters it acts on are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reckless behaviour by a rioter is a sorry business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturber of peace' reads as a rowdy, but disturber is the anagram signal working on PEACE and SAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a reckless or giddy adventure, exactly the kind of irresponsible behaviour called flighty conduct.

clue.text: In these columns, feature turns up on flowers

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters climb from bottom to top

blocks.note: a lip is a facial feature
asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A newspaper's columns run an item on flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' looks like newspaper columns; it means architectural ones. LIP read upwards then ASTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilasters are flat rectangular columns set into a wall, so columns is a fair broad term for them.

clue.text: Book for entertainment?

blocks.note: surface reading: a verb, to reserve seats for a show
setter's reading: the text of an opera or musical, written to be set to music

explanation.surface: Reserve tickets for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Book is a noun, not a verb: the book of a musical is its script.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto, Italian for little book, is the text of an opera or musical, the words a stage show is built on.

clue.text: Girl makes another carry on in charge

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: another girl's name
taken as written
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: One girl gets another to keep things going while she is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another girl: VERA holds ON + IC, giving VER + ONIC + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a woman's given name, so it is a fair example of the bare definition girl.

clue.text: Jim's address supplied by Conrad

blocks.note: surface reading: where someone called Jim lives, a postal address
setter's reading: the title Joseph Conrad gave his hero Jim in the 1900 novel, the form of address before his name

explanation.surface: A novelist hands over a friend's home address.
explanation.walkthrough: Address means a form of address, a title. Conrad's novel is called Lord Jim, after its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In Conrad's novel the hero is known as Lord Jim, so the title lord is the address the author gave him.

clue.text: The way the girl entered man's address

indicators.note: someone who enters goes inside, so this piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Mr is the form of address for a man
a girl's name

explanation.surface: How a girl came into the man's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Address means a form of address, not a home: Mr, with ANNE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner means the way something is done, as in a manner of speaking, so it substitutes for the way.

clue.text: Deity has strange head of this stone

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of order, so its letters are rearranged
the head of this answer is its opening, so the jumbled piece goes first

blocks.note: the word has, rearranged
a Lar was a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A god is said to have a weird stone head.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled HAS is put at the head of the answer, before the deity LAR. The Lares were the guardian gods of a Roman home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed building stone, or masonry made of it, so stone defines it.

clue.text: The main transport one set in the old railway

indicators.note: a thing set in something is placed inside it

blocks.note: the London and North Eastern Railway, one of Britain's big four lines before 1948
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sea transport for a drunk on the old railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, as in the Spanish Main. The page reads 'sot', a scan misread of 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, so it is transport across the main, the open sea.

clue.text: Transport man gets a morning to load the canopy

indicators.note: loading means putting cargo inside, so the canopy holds the other pieces

blocks.note: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed
taken as written
M is short for morning, as in a.m.

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is given one morning to load a tarpaulin cover.
explanation.walkthrough: TESTER holds A and M after its first two letters. A tester is an old word for a bed canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: A teamster is a truck driver, especially in America, and originally the driver of a team of horses: a man in haulage.

clue.text: Conspicuous success of £100 tea blend

indicators.note: a blend mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral 100 and L is the abbreviation for pounds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hundred-pound blend of tea becomes a striking commercial triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pounds comes from Latin libra, which is also where the £ sign comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant, showy success or acclaim, a French borrowing for dazzling achievement.

clue.text: Drive may get the batsman out?

blocks.note: first meaning: a short ride in a car for pleasure
second meaning: turn put on a ball by a cricket bowler, which can beat the batsman and dismiss him

explanation.walkthrough: A drive is also a cricket stroke, which tempts you towards a batting word; here it is a jaunt in a car. In cricket, spin bowling is a common way of getting a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a brief outing in a car, and spin bowling turns the ball off the pitch and can dismiss a batsman.

clue.text: Dance with Jack before everyone returns

indicators.note: a word that returns comes back the way it came, written right to left

blocks.note: jack and tar are both slang for a sailor
ante is Latin for before
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A dance partnered with Jack before all the guests come back.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling folk dance from southern Italy, so it is a particular kind of dance.

clue.text: Islanders find youth leader in the tropics, possibly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: the first letter of youth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Island people come across a young leader somewhere hot, near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: The tropics suggests a location for the islanders, but the word itself is raw material for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypriots are the people of Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean, so they are islanders.

clue.text: Flushing, perhaps — the unfinished naval base

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: flushing cheeks are pink and glowing
the word the, cut short

explanation.surface: Flushing, the Dutch port, might be a half-built navy base.
explanation.walkthrough: Flushing (Vlissingen) is a real Dutch port, which is the trap; here it means going red. Rosyth is the Royal Navy dockyard on the Firth of Forth in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosyth in Fife was a principal Royal Navy dockyard, so it is a specific example of a naval base.
